title: A sub-plan that needs a value
idea: TOOL: a parameter lets a sub-plan take a value when you call it, so each call can differ.

exercises.prompt: def greet() always prints the same 'Hi'. To greet a SPECIFIC score each time, the sub-plan needs...
options: a value handed in when you call it
exercises.explanation: A sub-plan that should change per call needs information passed in. That slot is called a parameter.

exercises.prompt:
Look:

def show_score(points):
    print(points)

What is 'points'?
options: a parameter - a slot for a value handed in
exercises.explanation: 'points' is a parameter: a named slot. When you call show_score, you hand it a value for points.

exercises.prompt: You call show_score(10). What does the body print?
exercises.explanation: The 10 goes into the parameter points, so print(points) shows 10. The call supplies the value.

exercises.prompt: A parameter lets the SAME sub-plan behave differently depending on the value you give it.
exercises.explanation: Yes. show_score(10) prints 10; show_score(7) prints 7. One definition, different values per call.

options: One sub-plan handles many values instead of one fixed value
It removes the need to call
exercises.explanation: Without parameters you'd need a separate sub-plan per value. A parameter lets one sub-plan serve all values.

exercises.prompt: Match each call to what show_score(points) prints.
exercises.explanation: The value in the call fills the parameter, and the body prints it. Each call can carry a different value.

exercises.prompt: The value you put in the call, like the 10 in show_score(10), is called...
exercises.explanation: The value handed in is the argument; the slot that receives it is the parameter. 10 is the argument here.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: you still need both a def (to define) and a call (to run) - parameters just add a value to the call.
exercises.explanation: Yes. def+call from last unit still apply. A parameter adds a value slot; the argument fills it on the call.

exercises.prompt: This idea matches which thinking lesson from before?
options: 'sub-plans that need information' - handing values to a job
exercises.explanation: You met the idea conceptually. Now parameters are the real code for handing a job the values it needs.

exercises.prompt: The new tool this unit adds on top of def and call is...
options: parameters - a way to hand values into a sub-plan
exercises.explanation: Parameters let a sub-plan accept values when called, so one definition can work for many inputs.
